subject: QuantumCore Dedicated: burst mitigation, autoscale ops & amendment
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@quantumcore.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QuantumCore Dedicated: burst mitigation, autoscale ops & amendment

Sara — thanks again for the deep dive this morning. Per our conversation, I'm sending a concise ops-focused proposal for how Redwood would handle short-duration burst events for your Dedicated pool and the autoscale behavior we recommend to balance cost vs. SLOs.

Key asks from your side: confirm target P95 latency (currently you told us ~150ms for gen workloads), and whether you need standby headroom guaranteed for marketing spikes (weekend campaigns).

Proposal highlights (attachments below):
- Commit: Reserved slab sized for base sustained throughput (we propose 64 A100-equivalent slots for the committed pool).
- Burst model: Opportunistic shoulder pool that can scale up to +40% for short windows with pre-emptible instances.
- Autoscale policy: Tiered scale-in where headroom is not fully reclaimed for 10 minutes after peak to avoid oscillation; priority-capped eviction for best-effort jobs.
- Fallback: Canary route to the smaller quantized model (q2) when pre-emptible capacity is exhausted to maintain P95 with higher token-cost efficiency.

Attachments: [attachment: burst-sim-forecast-v2.xlsx (xlsx, 1.1 MB)], [attachment: dedicated-autoscale-config.yaml (yaml, 3.4 KB)]

Next steps: if this looks good, we'll draft the amendment and include the burst SLA appendix and a simple crediting formula for missed sustained capacity during the ramp window. Can we schedule a 30-min ops alignment on Thursday PST?

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: burst-sim-forecast-v2.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuantumCore Dedicated: burst mitigation, autoscale ops & amendment

Chloe — looping in more detail on the technical controls. See inline and config notes.

Inline: 
- Headroom multiplier: recommend conservative 1.35x for sustained CPU/GPU allocation for production LLM traffic; this includes buffer for short (<=5min) transient spikes.
- Pre-warm windows: schedule pre-warm for anticipated campaign windows (configurable cron on Redwood Console). Pre-warm should be considered "warm but idle" vs full KV-cache warm; add +6s cold-start reduction per pre-warmed instance in the estimates.
- Eviction policy: best-effort (non-reserved) jobs get lowest eviction priority; critical customer threads (pinned) are marked on the routing policy. We also prefer soft-eviction (requeue) vs hard-kill for longer-running batch embeddings.
- Autoscale hysteresis: scale-down delay = 600s, scale-up aggressive for 3 consecutive sampling intervals. Sampling interval default = 30s.

I've attached a trimmed config that we would push to the private control plane once QuantumCore signs the amendment: dedicated-autoscale-config.yaml

Testing notes: ran a 48-hr sim against your sample trace (see burst-sim-forecast-v2.xlsx). Results: median P95 latency stayed ~160ms with canary fallback enabled; cost uplift for peak windows estimated at +18% vs strictly reserved capacity.

Action items for ops meeting:
- Confirm accepted headroom multiplier (1.35 vs 1.25).
- Decide whether QuantumCore wants credits for unmet headroom (tiered: full credit if sustained >10m continuous shortage).
- Agree on monitoring hooks (we will expose per-route token-level telemetry and a burst-capacity metric).

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Capacity Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@quantumcore.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@quantumcore.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuantumCore Dedicated: burst mitigation, autoscale ops & amendment

Chloe / team — thanks for the clear write-up. A couple of clarifications from our side before the Thursday sync: 
1) For the headroom multiplier, quantumcore prefers 1.25x if it reduces our committed monthly spend materially. Can you quantify the cost delta in the spreadsheet with 1.25 vs 1.35?
2) We need the crediting formula spelled out in contract terms. The idea is simple: if we experience a sustained period >10m where pre-agreed headroom is insufficient and the fallback triggers, we get a pro-rata credit on that portion of the month. Will legal accept a specific measurement query?

Also procurement wants to confirm the maximum burst cap (is +40% hard or soft?). If pre-emptible inventory is exhausted, what is the deterministic failover path?

Can do Thursday 10:00 AM PST. Add me and procurement.

—Sara
Sara Kim
VP Product, QuantumCore

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@quantumcore.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuantumCore Dedicated: burst mitigation, autoscale ops & amendment

Sara / team — quick ops clarifications ahead of today's call. Answers below: 
- +40% is a soft cap for opportunistic pre-emptible capacity; we will surface a deterministic fallback order: (1) pre-warmed pre-emptible slots in the shoulder pool, (2) opportunistic cloud GPU inventory, (3) route to q2 quantized model on the same pool, (4) cross-region failover (only if you opt in).
- Crediting: we can implement a queryable metric (burst_shortfall_seconds_by_route) and a simple pro-rata monthly credit for uncovered sustained shortage minutes beyond the 10m threshold. We'll draft language for procurement but the mechanics are straightforward to measure.
- Cost delta: Karthik, can you add a second tab with the 1.25x vs 1.35x cost comparison and the estimated monthly committed price delta? Chloe, I'll flag this during contract negotiations as an optional tier.

Operational note — for auditability we will ship a weekly CSV export of capacity-events and a linkable per-incident trace in the Console.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachments: qcore-amendment-draft.docx
